correctness.rationale: For every element alpha*1+j in the radical J, its square is 2alpha element-alpha^2; the subalgebra Im R cannot contain a nonzero scalar part, else 1 lies in Im R, impossible by the weight-zero RB identity. With Im R contained in J and J-elements anticommuting, the identity on (a,a) gives R²=0; therefore rank<=2. Rank-two image=kernel is a 2D subalgebra W of J, necessarily span(u,z), and automorphisms normalize W=span(y,z). The full stabilizer conjugation on matrix M=[[a,c],[b,d]] was derived independently and its transformed determinant equals u² det M. Splitting invertible matrices into a!=0,c=0, a=0,c!=0 and a,c!=0 leaves invariants d/a, sign(bc), and det M/a², giving the three complete strata. Rank-one maps f(.)v must annihilate vE+Ev, yielding precisely three socle-image and three degree-one-image classes. The packaged symbolic script was inspected; independent symbolic stabilizer checks corroborate, not replace, the orbit completeness proof.

value.rationale: For a fixed natural 4D associative algebra, an exact moduli problem under its actual automorphisms is structural: two copies of R× plus two sign orbits and six discrete rank-one orbits classify genuinely different operators; the field-sensitive sign stratum is a motivated distinction, not an arbitrary numeric census.

final_claim: For weight-zero Rota-Baxter maps on E=Lambda_R(R^2), every R squares to zero and has rank<=2. Up to algebra-automorphism conjugation there are six nonzero rank-one orbits and rank-two orbits of types A_t,C_t (t real nonzero) and B_sigma (sigma=+/-1), with unique parameters.
